title: Service account key file: private key as a JSON string
summary: A synthetic Google service account key file whose private_key field holds a PEM block as one JSON string with escaped newlines, beside public-looking identifying fields (project_id, client_email, client_id, key id, certificate URLs).
rationale: The secret sits inside a JSON string where the PEM line breaks are the two characters backslash and n, so a line-oriented PEM reading never sees the block as lines. Reporting only the identifying fields, or only the BEGIN marker, would leave the key body exposed. The embedded PEM grammar is the existing generic:private-key family (#54); this case adds the file-level extent.

expectation.rationale: Flag, with the private_key string value (the whole PEM block as it appears inside the JSON string) as the secret extent. Google names PRIVATE_KEY in the key file as the private portion of the key pair and says to store the file securely because anyone who finds it can use the service account. Whether the BEGIN and END marker lines are part of the minimal extent is not stated; the span covers the whole string value.

sources.supports: The downloaded key has the following format, where PRIVATE_KEY is the private portion of the public/private key pair.

Always store your service account keys in a secure location. If you don't store your keys securely, then bad actors can find the keys and use them to access the resources that the service account can access.
